associations.name: Pensacola
associations.associationType: Historical Panzacola people connection in original scholarly research
associations.period: Seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, especially documentary accounts of the 1680s–1690s
associations.sourceTitle: Patrick Anthony DeRoche — In Pursuit of the Panzacola: A Historical Documentary and Archaeological Investigation
associations.sourceDate: Thesis title page 2024; repository-generated cover cites 2025; document version labeled preprint
associations.evidenceNote: DeRoche’s introduction explicitly places the historical Panzacola people around present-day Pensacola Bay in West Florida using seventeenth-century documentary accounts. His discussion distinguishes this people from the archaeological Pensacola culture; the test excavation did not establish a positive Panzacola site identification.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual university public download, valid-TLS HTTP 200, 2,675,875 bytes, 100 PDF pages including added cover. Cover/title; abstract printed p.viii / PDF p.9; introduction printed pp.1–3 / PDF pp.10–12; and printed p.8 / PDF p.17 were read as text/OCR. Not a complete thesis or excavation-data review.
limits: The canonical name Pensacola is retained; Panzacola is the historical people-label used by the thesis. The later city and archaeological culture are separate referents.
No definitive excavated Panzacola village, coordinates, ethnicity-from-ceramics inference, contemporary recognition status or disappearance claim is adopted.
This is an original student thesis with committee oversight, not a statement of consensus on every historical identification.
